# impair

A React framework that holds state in class-based services managed by a dependency container, and lets React be the View layer. Components are declarative and stateless; services hold and mutate state via reactive class fields. Components re-render automatically when fields they read change.

Repository: https://github.com/kutlugsahin/impair
Examples: `examples/` directory in this repository — each numbered folder is a single-concept example.

## Install

```bash
npm install impair reflect-metadata
```

```jsonc
// tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "emitDecoratorMetadata": true,
    "experimentalDecorators": true
  }
}
```

```ts
// main.tsx — must be first import
import 'reflect-metadata'
```

```ts
// vite.config.ts — SWC variant
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react-swc'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react({ tsDecorators: true })],
  esbuild: { tsconfigRaw: { compilerOptions: { experimentalDecorators: true } } },
})
```

## Mental model

- **Services** are `@injectable()` classes registered in a `ServiceProvider`. One instance per container by default (`singleton`).
- **View models** are `@injectable()` classes scoped to a single component, instantiated via `useViewModel`. Each component instance gets its own.
- **Reactivity** is per-field via `@state`. Reading a field inside a `component(...)`-wrapped function subscribes that render to changes.
- **Side effects** in services/VMs use `@trigger` (runs on read deps changing) or `@onMount` / `@onInit`.
- **Containers form a hierarchy** through React context — child containers can resolve from any ancestor.

## API surface

### Decorators (class-level)

- `@injectable()` — required on every class managed by the container.
- `@provide(registrations)` — view model class decorator. Adds registrations to the per-component container before the VM is resolved.

### Decorators (field/getter)

- `@state` / `@state.deep` — deeply reactive field. Mutations to nested properties trigger updates.
- `@state.shallow` — first-level reactivity only.
- `@state.atom` — reactive on reassignment only.
- `@derived` — getter decorator. Computed value cached until upstream `@state` changes.

### Decorators (method)

- `@trigger` — runs immediately on first resolution, then **synchronously** every time any reactive read inside the body changes. Optional `Cleanup` param fires before each re-run and on disposal.
- `@trigger.async` — same dependency tracking, but the call is deferred to the next microtask. Multiple `@state` mutations made in the same synchronous block coalesce into a **single** run on the final values. Use it whenever one method flips several reactive fields that all feed the same effect.
- `@trigger.debounce(ms)` — trailing-only debounce. Re-runs `ms` after the most recent dependency change; bursts of changes inside the window collapse to one run on the final state. Use for "wait until the input settles" cases (typeahead, autosave on idle, resize-end recompute). Initial run is immediate.
- `@trigger.throttle(ms)` — leading + trailing throttle. Fires immediately on the first change in a window, then at most one trailing run per `ms` if more changes arrive. Use for "give me regular updates while it's still moving" cases (scroll/drag-driven UI, telemetry). Initial run is immediate.
- `@onInit` / `@onDispose` — fires when the instance is constructed / when its container is disposed. Optional `Cleanup`.
- `@onMount` / `@onUnmount` — fires when the host React component mounts / unmounts. Optional `Cleanup` on `@onMount`.

### Decorators (constructor parameter)

- `@inject(token)` — `token` is a class, string, or `Symbol`. Use `@inject(delay(() => SomeClass))` to break circular dependencies (impair injects a proxy until the cycle resolves).

### Hooks

- `useService<T>(ClassOrToken)` — resolves from the current container or any ancestor. By default returns a read-only proxy (configurable).
- `useViewModel<T>(VMClass)` — instantiates VM in the per-component container, shared across all `useViewModel` / `useResolve` calls within the same component. Throws if not inside a `component(...)` wrapper.
- `useResolve<T>(Class, props?)` — creates a fresh transient instance per call site. Calling it more than once in the same component yields **independent** instances (one of the few things `useViewModel` cannot do). Props (if provided) are exposed to that instance via the `Props` token.

  ```ts
  // three independent FieldViewModels in one component
  const email    = useResolve(FieldViewModel, { initial: '', validate: emailRule })
  const password = useResolve(FieldViewModel, { initial: '', validate: passwordRule })
  const code     = useResolve(FieldViewModel, { initial: '', validate: codeRule })
  ```

### Components

- `component(fn)` — wraps a function component, returning a memoized reactive component. Required for any component that reads reactive state.
  - `Comp.provide(...registrations)` — returns a variant whose contents see those services in scope.
- `component.fromViewModel(VMClass)` — turns a VM with a `render(): ReactElement` method into a component. The VM is its own renderer.
- `ServiceProvider` — registers services into a new container and provides it through context. Props: `provide: Registration[]`, `props?: object`, `initializeSingletons?: boolean`.

### Injection tokens

- `Props` — the `props` object passed to `ServiceProvider` or the React props of a `component(...)`-wrapped component, exposed as a shallowly reactive object.
- `Container` — handle to the current container; supports `.resolve(token)` / `.register(...)`.

### Utilities

- `configure({ readonlyProxiesForView?, defaultStateReactiveLevel? })` — call once at app boot.
- `createDecorator((instance, key, reactivity) => Dispose | void)` — build a custom field decorator. `reactivity` exposes Vue primitives (`ref`, `effect`, `computed`, etc.).
- `toRaw(reactive)` — unwrap a reactive proxy to access the underlying object.
- `useReactiveObject(obj)` — make a plain object into a stable shallowly reactive object that tracks the latest values.
- `untrack(fn)` / `pauseTracking()` / `enableTracking()` — escape hatches for dependency collection.
- `inject`, `delay` — re-exported from `tsyringe`.

### Registration forms (`provide: Registration[]`)

```ts
// 1. Class — singleton
provide={[TodoService]}

// 2. [Class, Lifecycle]
provide={[[TodoService, 'transient']]}

// 3. [Token, Class] — token resolves to singleton instance of Class
provide={[['todoApi', TodoApi]]}

// 4. [Token, Class, Lifecycle]
provide={[['todoApi', TodoApi, 'resolution']]}

// 5. RegistrationObject — value/factory provider
provide={[{
  token: 'apiToken',
  provider: { useValue: 'Bearer ...' },
  lifecycle: 'singleton',
}]}

// 6. [Token, plainObject] — exposed as a shallow reactive object
provide={[['config', { theme: 'dark' }]]}
```

Lifecycles: `'singleton' | 'transient' | 'container' | 'resolution'`.

## Patterns

### Counter (smallest VM)
```ts
@injectable()
class CounterViewModel {
  @state count = 0
  increment() { this.count++ }   // plain method — impair auto-binds at construction
}

const Counter = component(() => {
  // Destructure freely — reactive reads are tracked at the moment of access in render,
  // and methods are pre-bound so `onClick={increment}` works without `.bind(vm)`.
  const { count, increment } = useViewModel(CounterViewModel)
  return <button onClick={increment}>{count}</button>
})
```

### Service shared across components
```tsx
<ServiceProvider provide={[ApiClient, CartService]}>
  <Cart />
  <Checkout />
</ServiceProvider>

// any descendant component — destructure the parts you actually use
const { items, addItem, removeItem } = useService(CartService)
```

### Trigger with cleanup (cancel in-flight on dep change)
```ts
@trigger
async loadUser(cleanup: Cleanup) {
  const controller = new AbortController()
  cleanup(() => controller.abort())
  this.user = await fetch(`/users/${this.props.userId}`, { signal: controller.signal })
}
```

### Component props into a view model
```ts
@injectable()
class UserViewModel {
  constructor(@inject(Props) private props: { userId: number }) {}

  @trigger
  load() { /* re-runs whenever props.userId changes */ }
}

const UserCard = component<{ userId: number }>(() => {
  const vm = useViewModel(UserViewModel)
  return <div>{vm.user?.name}</div>
})
```

### Derived state
```ts
@injectable()
class TodoService {
  @state todos: Todo[] = []
  @derived get completed() { return this.todos.filter(t => t.done) }
  @derived get pendingCount() { return this.todos.length - this.completed.length }
}
```

### Narrow a trigger's deps with `untrack`
A `@trigger` subscribes to every reactive read inside it. Wrap reads in `untrack(() => ...)` when you want the *current value* of a field without making it a dependency. Classic case: autosave that reacts to content changes but uses the *current* author/session at the moment of save.
```ts
@trigger
autoSave() {
  const content = this.draft                          // tracked → re-runs on draft change
  const by      = untrack(() => this.currentUser)     // not tracked → won't re-trigger
  save({ content, by })
}
```

### Lifecycle
```ts
@onMount
async load(cleanup: Cleanup) {
  const controller = new AbortController()
  cleanup(() => controller.abort())
  this.todos = await this.api.fetch({ signal: controller.signal })
}
```

### View model as the renderer (`fromViewModel`)
```ts
@injectable()
class TimerViewModel implements RendererViewModel {
  @state seconds = 0

  @onMount
  start(cleanup: Cleanup) {
    const h = setInterval(() => this.seconds++, 1000)
    cleanup(() => clearInterval(h))
  }

  render() { return <div>{this.seconds}s</div> }
}

export const Timer = component.fromViewModel(TimerViewModel)
```

## Conventions

- **Declare service / view-model behaviour as normal class methods**, not arrow-function fields. impair auto-binds every prototype method to the instance at construction time, so `onClick={vm.increment}` works without explicit `.bind`. Arrow-function fields work but cost an allocation per instance and bypass the auto-bind path.

  ```ts
  // ✅ idiomatic
  class CounterViewModel {
    @state count = 0
    increment() { this.count++ }
  }

  // ❌ avoid — extra allocation, redundant with auto-bind
  class CounterViewModel {
    @state count = 0
    increment = () => { this.count++ }
  }
  ```

- **Destructure the hook return.** Reactive reads are tracked at the moment of access during render, so pulling `count`/`increment`/etc. out of `useService` / `useViewModel` / `useResolve` does not break reactivity. Prefer this for readability.

  ```ts
  const { count, increment } = useViewModel(CounterViewModel)
  ```

  Caveat: don't destructure *deep* into reactive objects — `const { name } = vm.user` will not re-render when `vm.user` becomes a different object. Destructure top-level only.

## Pitfalls

- **Wrap components with `component()`** if they read reactive state, otherwise they will not re-render on mutation.
- **Mutate from services, not from JSX.** Reactive fields exposed to components are read-only proxies by default. Call a method on the service instead. (Set `readonlyProxiesForView: false` in `configure()` to disable, but it's safer left on.)
- **Class identity matters.** `useService(TodoService)` resolves by class reference. Two `class TodoService {}` declarations in different files are different tokens. Import the class from one canonical module.
- **HMR**: editing a service file invalidates importers transitively until a refresh boundary is hit. Modules that aren't re-evaluated keep the old class reference and will resolve a detached instance. Prefer string/`Symbol` tokens for boundaries where this matters.
- **`useViewModel` only inside `component(...)`-wrapped components.** Calling it from a plain function component throws.
- **Triggers run synchronously on every dep change.** Use `@trigger.async` when a single method assigns several `@state` fields that all feed the trigger — sync would fire once per assignment, observing intermediate (often invalid) snapshots; async runs once on the final values.
- **Circular service deps** require `@inject(delay(() => OtherService))` on at least one side, otherwise the container loops infinitely during construction.
- **`@state` defaults to deep tracking.** For large objects or maps where you only mutate the reference, use `@state.atom` / `@state.shallow` to avoid proxy overhead.
- **`onMount` ≠ `onInit`.** `@onInit` runs when the instance is constructed (which may be lazily on first resolve). `@onMount` runs when the host React component mounts. For service-layer side effects tied to UI lifetime, prefer `@onMount`.
